title: The Last Echo Again
premise: Rafael Reyes, the last employee of a dissolved insurance syndicate, tends a deep-space beacon whose founding records were deliberately erased. When a distress call arrives in the extinct Meridian tongue, he deciphers it and learns the beacon exists to perpetuate a two-century-old lie: a fabricated atrocity that keeps the Meridian remnant fleet and the Concord navy from open war. As a Concord salvage squadron and a Meridian ghost ship both converge on the beacon, Rafael must decide whether to broadcast the truth and ignite a war, or preserve the lie and let the beacon's failing reactor kill them all. He ends the countdown by fusing his own recorded memories into the beacon, creating a living archive that both fleets can verify — and in doing so, he becomes the last echo himself.
about_author: Rosalind Hartwell is a former maritime insurance adjuster from Bristol who turned to science fiction after a career spent investigating losses no one wanted to explain. Her novels explore the paperwork of catastrophe — the forms, beacons, and omissions that outlive the people who filed them.

chapters.title: The Quiet Asset
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On the beacon station Perpetuity, Rafael performs his annual maintenance ritual, logging hours for a syndicate that no longer exists to pay him. He discovers a sealed compartment in the reactor housing he has never seen before. Emotional beat: lonely routine cracked open by a first anomaly.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A distress transmission arrives, and Rafael's inherited linguistic archive identifies it as Meridian — extinct since the Silence Accords. The signal is addressed to the beacon itself, not to him. Emotional beat: vertigo of being spoken to across two centuries.

chapters.title: The File That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with flashbacks to his predecessor Voss. Rafael searches the station archives for the beacon's founding charter and finds every record redacted in the same hand. Voss's final log hints: 'Some premiums are paid in silence.' Emotional beat: the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Decoding fragments, Rafael reconstructs the core deception: the Meridian 'massacre' that justified the Accords never happened as recorded; the beacon was built to keep the forged evidence intact. Emotional beat: horrified comprehension of his custodianship.

chapters.title: The Concord Salvage Squadron
chapters.summary: Squadron Captain Ilsa Vey's POV. The Concord warship Meridian's Wake detects the beacon's anomalous transmission and diverts to investigate, under sealed orders Rafael cannot imagine. Emotional beat: duty sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ghost Ship Rising
chapters.summary: Meridian archivist Sen Oduya's POV. Aboard the derelict fleet ship Long Remembrance, Sen decodes the same distress call and convinces her dying crew to make one final burn toward the beacon — the last address their language still knows. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into hope.

chapters.title: Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The sealed compartment turns out to hold the reactor's original failsafe, now tripped by the distress signal's handshake: sixty days to detonation unless a valid Meridian cipher disarms it. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Vey Arrives
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Vey. Vey's squadron docks under pretense of inspection; Rafael hides the Meridian signal and the failsafe. Their cat-and-mouse interview is courteous and lethal. Emotional beat: two professionals lying fluently to each other.

chapters.title: Sen's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sen's POV. The Long Remembrance reaches beacon space and is immediately targeted by Vey's weapons. Sen transmits the Meridian cipher publicly, gambling that truth will protect them. Emotional beat: desperate courage.

chapters.title: The Cipher That Kills
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Sen's transmission is authentic but incomplete — it accelerates the countdown instead of stopping it. Rafael realizes the failsafe demands a full cipher held only by the beacon's erased founders. Emotional beat: the rescue becomes the crisis.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Records
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Vey's own intelligence officer reveals Concord command has known about the forged atrocity for decades and wants the beacon destroyed before anyone else can verify it. Vey must choose her orders or her oath. Emotional beat: loyalty fracturing under truth.

chapters.title: What Voss Knew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Deep in the station's sublevels, Rafael finds Voss's hidden study: the founder's confession, the full cipher in fragments, and evidence that the founders were Meridian survivors who built the lie to prevent a war both sides had already lost. Emotional beat: pity replacing betrayal.

chapters.title: The Long Remembrance Boards
chapters.summary: Sen and Rafael's POV. Sen's boarding party meets Rafael in the dark of the station; initial hostility gives way to shared decoding of the cipher fragments. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing a common inheritance.

chapters.title: Vey's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Ordered to fire on the station regardless of the reactor, Vey instead transmits a demand: surrender the archives or be destroyed. Rafael answers with the founder's confession, unencrypted, to both fleets at once. Emotional beat: truth as a thrown grenade.

chapters.title: War in Miniature
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Concord strike teams and Meridian defenders fight through the station corridors while the countdown drops below ten days. Rafael is wounded protecting the archive core. Emotional beat: the lie defending itself with human bodies.

chapters.title: The Incomplete Cipher
chapters.summary: Rafael and Sen's POV. The fragments are missing one component: a memory-verified attestation, a founder's lived recollection encoded in the beacon's original format. No founder remains. Emotional beat: the archive demands a witness.

chapters.title: Vey's Choice
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Vey refuses the destruction order and is deposed by her own executive officer, who prepares to fire. She escapes to the station with proof of Concord's cover-up. Emotional beat: treason as fidelity.

chapters.title: The Witness Standard
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael realizes the beacon's attestation protocol will accept any verified human memory recorded in its format — including his. But the recording process will fuse his neural archive into the station permanently. Emotional beat: the price made explicit.

chapters.title: Ten Minutes
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax POV. With the strike team firing and the countdown in its final minutes, Rafael records his memories of every person he's met aboard — Voss, Sen, Vey — while Sen and Vey hold the archive room. Emotional beat: sacrifice as testimony.

chapters.title: The Last Echo
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, dissolving. The cipher completes; the failsafe disarms; Rafael's consciousness becomes the beacon's verification layer. His final transmission is his own voice reading the true history in both tongues. Emotional beat: transfiguration of a caretaker into a monument.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Open Ledger
chapters.summary: Sen and Vey's POV. Both fleets receive the verified archive; the forged atrocity is formally retracted, and the Accords are renegotiated around shared truth. Sen and Vey, once enemies, co-author the new charter. Emotional beat: exhausted, cautious peace.

chapters.title: Perpetuity
chapters.summary: Sen's POV, epilogue. Years later, Sen visits the beacon and speaks to it in Meridian. It answers in Rafael's voice — not a ghost, but a record that listens. The station's registry now lists its keeper: R. Reyes, in perpetuity. Emotional beat: inheritance completed, loneliness answered.
